title: NovaQuark renewal + capacity uplift and EU edge / on-prem pathway
summary: Renewal check with NovaQuark: customer is evaluating a 2x capacity uplift, adding EU region with private VPC/on-prem option for regulated workloads, and discussing a 12-month extension. Main asks: price band for committed GPU-hours, timeline for EU edge + air-gapped pilot, SOC2/KMS docs, and a small benchmark run (50k tokens/day) before handoff.
topics: EU region add-on vs on-prem pilot
SLA, security (SOC2, KMS), and data residency
next_steps: Jordan Hale - Send updated commitment pricing tiers and a side-by-side hosted vs dedicated cost comparison by 2026-10-18
Priya Raman - Schedule a 2-hour technical benchmark session with NovaQuark engineering (include perf matrix) week of 2026-10-25
Luis Ortega - Share SOC2 + KMS integration docs and draft on-prem checklist by 2026-10-20
Maya Chen - Confirm internal stakeholders and sign-off timeline by 2026-10-21
action_items: Maya - internal review & list of legal questions (due 2026-10-21)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hale (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (CTO, NovaQuark), Ethan Park (Head of ML), Sara Novak (Platform), Ravi Menon (Procurement)

Summary (auto): Renewal check, capacity scaling, EU region and on-prem pilot discussion.

00:00 Jordan Hale: Hey everyone, thanks for making time today, appreciate it. Quick roll call, we got Maya, Ethan, Sara, Ravi on the NovaQuark side?
00:05 Maya Chen: Yep hi Jordan, hi Priya, Luis. Morning for us, afternoon for you.
00:08 Ethan Park: Hi all.
00:10 Priya Raman: Hey — glad to be here. Wanted to dig into the capacity numbers and the EU/on-prem options.
00:18 Jordan Hale: Perfect. Agenda — quick recap of current usage, proposed uplift and regions, security & on-prem path, then next steps and timelines. Sound good?
00:25 Maya Chen: Sounds good. Quick context: we're mid-Q4 planning, want to nail a contract by end of Oct so engineering can schedule the pilot in November.
00:33 Jordan Hale: Great. Can you run through current usage and where pain points are?
00:38 Ethan Park: Sure. We're currently provisioned at a committed Dedicated pool that covers about 120 GPU-hours/day equivalent for our inf serv. Average latency is okay but peak traffic during batch jobs spikes CPU and we see queuing. Tokens/day on production are roughly 1.2M with embeddings and chat loads combined. We expect that to double next quarter as we add two more product features.
01:00 Priya Raman: When you say queuing, is that mostly at the prefix stage or KV cache misses?
01:06 Ethan Park: Mostly KV misses during long-form generation, and also end-of-day batch reindexing. So high tail latency.
01:12 Sara Novak: And we have strict residency needs for EU customers — anything with PII has to be processed on EU infra or on-prem. That’s a hard constraint.
01:21 Jordan Hale: Understood. So high-level ask: 2x capacity reserved, plus EU region activation and an on-prem pilot for regulated flow. Is that accurate?
01:29 Maya Chen: Yes. And pricing needs to be predictable — procurement is looking for a commitment price band for 12 months.
01:36 Ravi Menon: We also need clarity on SLA uplifts and outage credit language if we go to dedicated reserved.
01:43 Priya Raman: We'll cover SLA. On the EU piece — we offer hosted EU regions, private VPCs, and an on-prem/offline pilot for air-gapped requirements. The difference is in data plane control and support footprint.
01:55 Maya Chen: Can you do on-prem for a subset of traffic? We don't need everything on-prem, just the regulated pipelines.
02:01 Priya Raman: Absolutely, that's the normal approach — hybrid routing rules. We can route regulated jobs to the on-prem cluster, and the rest to hosted/dedicated in EU.
02:09 Ethan Park: Technical question — how does KV cache behave across the hybrid boundary? Will we suffer cache misses on the on-prem lane?
02:16 Priya Raman: Good point. On-prem will have a local KV store for low-latency access. Cross-boundary cache hits won't be guaranteed; we typically recommend a prefix-caching strategy and warmup for common prompts. For the regulated set, you get the latency benefits of local cache.
02:29 Luis Ortega: There's also quantization and model variant recommendations — if you go with a smaller quantized variant for on-prem you might reduce GPU footprint substantially. We can surface specific tradeoffs in the benchmark.
02:38 Maya Chen: Speaking of benchmarks, we want a short perf run — targeted: 50k tokens/day for two weeks against our top prompt templates. Can Redwood run that in a sandbox so we can compare hosted vs dedicated vs on-prem?
02:50 Jordan Hale: Yes, we can set up a controlled benchmark. Priya — we'll need the prompt set and the pass/fail criteria.
02:55 Priya Raman: I'll take point. Send over the templates and we'll draft a runbook. Expect a 2-hour kickoff with your engineers to instrument metrics.
03:04 Sara Novak: On the security side: SOC2, KMS, encryption-in-transit, audit logs — we need documentation and also an on-prem checklist (HSM/KMS integration details).
03:14 Luis Ortega: We'll share our SOC2 report and a KMS integration guide. For on-prem HSM we'd need to validate supported vendors; we support common ones via our KMS connector but the air-gapped setup has a few manual steps.
03:25 Ravi Menon: Legal will want to see indemnity and data residency clauses. Can you share a draft MSA with proposed residency language?
03:31 Jordan Hale: Yes, we'll include a residency addendum and proposed SLA terms. We'll also present pricing bands for committed GPU-hours for 12 months.
03:38 Maya Chen: Pricing — we need at least two options: conservative (1.5x) and aggressive (2x) capacity, with clear uplift for EU and additional for on-prem support (professional services). Also, what's the lead time for EU region activation if we choose hosted EU?
03:50 Priya Raman: Hosted EU region activation is usually 2-3 weeks for standard onboarding if it's a new region for the account, less if you already have reserved capacity in other regions. On-prem pilot is longer — typically 6-8 weeks for air-gapped validation plus procurement.
04:04 Ethan Park: That timeline is tight for our November pilot. Is there a fast path?
04:08 Priya Raman: Fast path: spin up a dedicated EU hosted pool (we can enable within 7-10 business days with a rush request), run the benchmark there, while we run the on-prem pilot in parallel as a follow-up. That way you get the EU residency test sooner.
04:20 Maya Chen: That seems okay, we can accept hosted EU for the first pass. Cost matters though. How much more expensive is rush activation and having both hosted EU + on-prem later?
04:29 Jordan Hale: I'll model that in the pricing worksheet — separate line items for rush activation, dual-routes, and on-prem professional services. We'll also show committed vs pay-as-you-go margins.
04:36 Ravi Menon: Another procurement item — are there early termination clauses if we mis-estimate capacity? We need flexibility for a short-term cushion.
04:43 Jordan Hale: We can discuss staged commitments — 6 months guaranteed with a 12-month extension option, or commit to full 12 months with a stepped ramp schedule. We'll propose both in the quote.
04:53 Priya Raman: On load shaping: we can provide auto-burst capacity for spikes; that’s priced differently but can be set to fallback to a lower-cost variant during sustained load.
05:02 Ethan Park: Curious about model variants — can you pin different versions per route? e.g., v1.2 on hosted EU, v1.3 quantized on-prem?
05:09 Priya Raman: Yes, model pinning per route is supported. You can also configure rollout policies and automatic fallbacks. We'll detail the model catalogue options available for your stack.
05:20 Sara Novak: For the bench: we need token accounting clarity — how tokens for embeddings vs chat are counted and billed in a hybrid run where some calls are on-prem and some in hosted.
05:29 Jordan Hale: We'll provide a breakdown in the pricing doc and show an estimated monthly burn for the proposed 2x uplift across usage profiles. The billing will aggregate at account level but we can tag by route for reporting.
05:39 Ravi Menon: About support SLAs — what does redwood promise on latency targets and incident response for dedicated pools?
05:45 Priya Raman: We have tiered SLAs. For dedicated pools with premium support, target p50/p95 latencies are guaranteed per-model profile, and incident response follows our enterprise playbook: 15-minute P1 detection, follow-up timelines, and credits for sustained downtime. We'll attach the SLA doc.
05:58 Maya Chen: Do you offer a two-week trial of the dedicated config before committing? We want to validate real traffic patterns.
06:04 Jordan Hale: We can do a short pilot under a pilot agreement — 30 days with prorated credits if you convert to a committed contract. That is often used for verifying tail latencies.
06:12 Ethan Park: That pilot would be great — we need to see the queuing behavior during end-of-day batch runs.
06:16 Priya Raman: We'll include batch test scenarios in the benchmark plan.
06:20 Luis Ortega: Also note that quantization/variant changes affect throughput and memory — we suggest a small POC to show cost delta per token.
06:29 Maya Chen: Cool. For the EU/on-prem gap — what kind of telemetry do we get from on-prem? We need tracing and token-level costs down to route.
06:36 Priya Raman: On-prem ships telemetry back to your control plane instance for metrics; for sensitive setups we can keep logs local and provide aggregated metrics. We'll propose a telemetry configuration that meets compliance.
06:48 Sara Novak: For KMS: we have a vendor preference (KeySafeCorp). Is that supported?
06:53 Luis Ortega: We have a connector for KeySafeCorp, but for air-gapped you'd run a local KMS that we integrate via secure API. We'll validate compatibility during the on-prem checklist.
06:59 Ravi Menon: Good. Anything else from Redwood side?
07:02 Jordan Hale: No — action items, we'll own pricing and the MSA draft. Priya will run the tech bench. Luis will send security docs. Maya, you'll confirm internal sign-off timeline.
07:10 Maya Chen: Yes, legal meets Friday; we'll try to get questions back by Oct 21.
07:14 Jordan Hale: Ok next — let's quickly walk through proposed timeline: if we sign LOI by Oct 22, we can activate hosted EU by early Nov. Benchmarks week of Nov 1, on-prem pilot start mid-November and finish early January. Does that align with your planning?
07:29 Maya Chen: That's tight but doable. Procurement needs a price term by Oct 18 to include in their board materials.
07:34 Jordan Hale: We'll prioritize the pricing doc to hit Oct 18.
07:37 Priya Raman: I'll send a benchmark kickoff calendar invite for the week of Oct 25 as discussed.
07:42 Ethan Park: Minor nit — we'd like to include a load-shaping policy in the SOW so we can avoid surprises when traffic spikes.
07:48 Jordan Hale: We'll include example autoscale and burst policies in the appendix.
07:52 Sara Novak: Can Redwood provide a short runbook for the on-prem install (hardware sku, network requirements) so our infra team can pre-approve hardware?
07:59 Priya Raman: Yes, we'll share a 1-page install checklist and minimal hardware profile. Might be options depending on model sizes.
08:06 Maya Chen: Great. Any immediate blockers?
08:09 Ravi Menon: Just procurement wants to know if there's any vendor lock concerns — can we export models and data if we leave?
08:16 Jordan Hale: Data egress is supported per the contract, and you can get a data export. Model weights depend on licencing of third-party models; for open models we can provide the artifacts, for proprietary variants we'll outline export rights. We'll clarify in the MSA.
08:30 Maya Chen: Ok that helps.
08:32 Jordan Hale: Alright let's recap next steps and owners. Jordan to send pricing by Oct 18; Priya to schedule bench and send runbook; Luis to send SOC2 & KMS docs by Oct 20; Maya to confirm internal timeline by Oct 21. Any other questions?
08:47 Ethan Park: No, thanks — excited to see the bench results.
08:50 Jordan Hale: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a meeting note and action items. Closing now.

End of transcript.
